item.title: Abandoned van at junction of gipsy road and Normanhurst avenue causing traffic hazard, 3rd August
item.description:
The vehicle, registration EU66 WVJ, has been parked in the same location on the public highway for approximately one year now (since July 2026 at least). Its MOT has expired, and no one in the neighbourhood appears to know who owns it. It appears to have been abandoned. It’s MOT has also expired since March 2026 In addition to being left in the same place for such a long period, the size of the van creates a significant visibility hazard. It obstructs drivers' sight lines, making it difficult for motorists to see approaching traffic and pedestrians when pulling out or passing by. There is also a school nearby (few mtrs down the road near coop), and this reduced visibility creates a potential safety risk for children, parents, pedestrians, and other road users, particularly during school drop-off and pick-up times. There have already been few incidents at the junction of Gipsy Road and Normanhurst avenue, most recently a street light pole was struck by a car at night (possibly due to poor visibility due to presence of this van) I would be grateful if the vehicle could be investigated as soon as possible and removed if appropriate.

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Normanhurst Avenue, West Heath, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet

item.title: Foundation damaged due to pothole, 3rd August
item.description:
I posted this last Thursday, but today the council sent me a confirmation saying the issue has been fixed, which is completely untrue. Anyway, I will keep reposting this until the work actually begins. Someone reported this pothole back in March, yet we are now approaching August and the Council has still done absolutely nothing to repair it. This is extremely disappointing and certainly gives residents reason to reconsider their support at the next local election. Since March, I have noticed that my house shakes significantly more every time buses drive through the pothole. I am becoming increasingly concerned that the continued deterioration of the road could eventually cause damage to nearby properties. Could someone please explain why no action has been taken despite the issue being reported several months ago? Are you waiting until the road collapses into a sinkhole or until properties are damaged before carrying out
Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): 97, Halfway Street, Longlands, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
